I am here in Mbeya, and the rains come well here — this is good maize country. My plot is small, just over half a hectare, and I have farmed it for many years. I went to school a little, so I know the names on the fertilizer bags, but my hands and my eyes tell me more than any paper. This season I will buy one bag of urea if the price at the dukas in town is not too high — my son sent me some money after the last harvest, so I have a little cash. I will also put the manure from my two goats on the plot before planting, like I did last year and the year before. I am old now, 76, so my two grandsons will help me with weeding — I cannot bend for long hours anymore.

I will plant the improved maize seed, the one my neighbor Mzee Mwakalinga used last season and got a good harvest — but I keep some of my old seed too, mixed in, because one never knows with the rains. I do not buy pesticides, the birds and small pests I chase away myself or the children do. No irrigation — the masika rains here are usually enough, and I have no pump, no river close by. Because I intercrop beans with the maize, the soil stays better and we eat from the same plot.
